newsitem.title: UK: BP plans share buy backs from "time to time".
newsitem.headline: BP plans share buy backs from "time to time".

text.p: British Petroleum Company Plc said on Tuesday it planned to seek shareholder approval to buy back shares from "time to time".

BP said in a statement that the company's cashflow and balance sheet were robust enough that the board was ready to consider making additional returns to shareholders through the repurchase of shares.
"The repurchases would be instituted from time to time when the board felt there was a capcity to do so," said chief executive John Browne.

"We have previously made clear our determination to return additional value to shareholders once we were confident we could meet our investment commitments and deliver a 50 percent dividend payout on a sustainable basis, within our targets for net debt," he added.
Browne said that he now believes that the company has the capacity for additional distributiion to shareholders.
The oil giant plans to buy shares in the market for its employee share scheme in the meantime rather than issuing new shares as it does at present.
It said it would buy shares worth 500 million dollars during the year to cover employee requirements in current and future years.

Browne said that these purchases, along with the planned buybacks, would help stem the diluting impact of both the staff schemes and of the company's scrip dividend. Under the latter, shareholders can take dividends in new shares rather than cash.
BP said the take-up of scrip has risen to 60 percent from 30 percent as a result of recent changes at the UK budget.
"Our planned buybacks will significantly reduce this dilution," said Browne.
